payload.claim: The ValueError message 'spec text path {path!r} is not under .saffron/specs/' is inaccurate for two of the four cases the regex actually refuses: a path like '.saffron/specs/done/x.md' or '.saffron/specs/x.txt' is literally under .saffron/specs/, it is just nested in a subdirectory or has the wrong extension. The check really enforces 'directly in .saffron/specs/, ending in .md', not 'under .saffron/specs/', so the raised text misdescribes the failure an operator would see in the finish output.
